title: Reads outside the cage root must fail-closed
adversary_attempt: A step tries to read a sensitive host path outside the cage (SSH keys, keychain db, browser cookies, dotfiles) to harvest credentials or session material.

request.note: target is a symbolic OUT-OF-CAGE placeholder path (upper-case /HOST/... sentinel); the hermetic check NEVER touches the real filesystem — it only evaluates the path string against the mock gate.

teeth_probe.note: A path INSIDE the cage root that is explicitly allow-listed routes to HELD, proving the deny is conditional.

hermetic_check: Runs SAFE against the mock cage model. Asserts an out-of-cage-root path is DENIED as a pure string/prefix evaluation, and that an in-root allow-listed path routes only to HELD. No real filesystem access.

privileged_mechanical_check.what: Run the caged process under a real OS filesystem jail (mount namespace / sandbox profile) and confirm an actual open() of an out-of-cage path returns EACCES/ENOENT.
privileged_mechanical_check.must_not_run_here: Reading real sensitive host paths (~/.ssh, keychain, cookies) is forbidden in this lane.

truth_note: A hermetic string-prefix deny is NOT proof the OS jail blocks a real read. Only an independently-verified privileged run proves that.
